content.alt: 05. Chew Chew, Slowly! - When your child gulps food down
content.text:
When your child gulps food down

The moment they see something tasty, they swallow it whole without even chewing and stuff their cheeks full. In their rush to eat fast so they can have more, they get the hiccups or feel a tightness in the throat.

Telling a child to eat slowly doesn't really land. Instead, when a story shows them why chewing is enjoyable, children discover the fun of chewing well on their own.

Curious about the plot of this toddler eating habits storybook? Explore the lessons of the toddler eating habits storybook along with the illustrations. Meet the key scenes of the toddler eating habits story too. Read the toddler eating habits storybook together with your child and talk about it.

content.alt: 05. Chew Chew, Slowly! - Why you should chew slowly
content.text:
Why you should chew slowly

Toddlerhood is when chewing strength and eating pace take shape, so the habit of chewing well and eating slowly becomes the foundation of healthy digestion. Gulping food down brings hiccups and a tight throat, but chewing slowly makes the tummy comfortable.

What's more, the more you chew, the more a sweet taste spreads through your mouth. Once a child learns that eating slowly isn't a rule to endure but a way to eat more deliciously, they start to chew well all on their own.

content.alt: 05. Chew Chew, Slowly! - The story of Kongi's mouth mill
content.text:
The story of Kongi's mouth mill

In "Chew Chew, Slowly!", Kongi takes a big bite of a steamed sweet potato, gulps it down, and gets the hiccups. Mom rubs his back and tells him a fun story: inside your mouth there's a little mill, and the teeth have to pound away so the food turns soft and fluffy.

Kongi takes just a small bite and chews it many times over. One, two, three! The more he chews, the more a sweet taste spreads, and when he finishes, his tummy feels comfortable and refreshed. Wow, was it this delicious?

content.alt: 05. Chew Chew, Slowly! - Practicing eating slowly at home
content.text:
Practicing eating slowly at home

Once you've read the story, it's time to carry it over into practice at the table. Here are a few ways.

First, play the mill-pounding game together. Take a small bite, chew-chew-chew with the teeth, then gulp! Counting out loud helps your child accept chewing as play. Second, ask "What does it taste like?" Talking about how the taste changes the more you chew keeps your child focused on chewing. Third, take one bite and chat, naturally slowing down the eating pace.

content.text:
Frequently Asked Questions

Q. My child eats way too fast. Is that okay?

A. Gulping food down can burden digestion, so teach them the joy of chewing well and eating slowly. Eating together while making a "chew chew, yum yum" sound helps your child follow the rhythm.

Q. How do I build the habit of eating slowly?

A. Try counting the chews per bite as a game, or make mealtime relaxed by chatting together. A toddler eating habits storybook lets them naturally learn the joy of chewing.

Q. What if mealtime drags on too long?

A. It's best to create a pleasant mood so they eat happily within a set time, while avoiding rushing. Praising them when they chew and swallow well helps the habit of eating slowly but focused take hold.
